result.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
result.summary: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 DiabAgent 研究套件，包含 APC 智能体框架、DiabetSim 患者模拟器和 SweetBench 基准，让模型借助医疗设备工具、依据持续观测推断个体状态并选择治疗动作，在 212 个血糖控制任务上评估闭环控制效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「高频规则控制＋低频智能体决策」的成本与性能权衡、以及从连续观测推断状态并决定何时干预，可能为 LVR 中动态计算、证据获取与停止决策的收益/成本分析提供类比性线索，但无视觉或 latent 表示内容，需较多核查。
